title: Public API re-exports lock jmap-types and jmap-base-client major versions
description:
src/lib.rs:29-33 and src/methods/mod.rs:18-21 — public re-exports lock this crate's API to the major versions of two upstream crates:

    pub use jmap_base_client::ClientError;
    pub use jmap_types::{AddedItem, ChangesResponse, GetResponse, QueryChangesResponse,
                         QueryResponse, SetError, SetResponse};

Also in the public signature of JmapMetadataExt::with_metadata_session at lib.rs:47:

    fn with_metadata_session(&self, session: jmap_base_client::Session) -> methods::SessionClient;

…the parameter type 'jmap_base_client::Session' is also pulled through the public API.

Once 0.1.0 ships:
- A major version bump of jmap-types (incompatible change to GetResponse, SetError, etc.) is a major-version bump of this crate.
- Same for jmap-base-client (Session, ClientError, JmapClient).
- Worse: a downstream consumer that uses 'jmap_metadata_client::ClientError' and 'jmap_base_client::ClientError' may now find both types but in TWO copies in the crate graph (different majors), with no compile-time guarantee they unify.

This is the standard 'pub use foo::Bar' versioning footgun called out in /review-library-supplement §versioning. Workspace AGENTS.md does NOT explicitly say all crates must hard-bump major versions together — though in practice all 30 crates are at 0.1.0 today and the workspace ships coordinated.

Possible mitigations:
(a) Document the major-version pin policy in README under 'Gotchas': 'this crate's major version is bumped in lockstep with jmap-types and jmap-base-client; do not depend on independent upgradability'.
(b) Add a 'cargo deny' or workspace check that pins all jmap-* to identical major versions.
(c) Replace re-exports with local newtypes for the smallest surface (ClientError) — but the larger types (GetResponse<T>, SetResponse<T>) would be hostile to newtype.

Recommendation: (a). Cheapest. Make the coupling explicit and document it. Lockstep-bump is already how the workspace operates; just say so in README.

Note: this is workspace-wide; canonical mail-client and every other extension client has the same exposure. Propagate the README convention.
close_reason: Triage 2026-10-31 at c07d5206: moot: metadata-client no longer re-exports jmap_types/jmap_base_client items or JmapMetadataExt::with_metadata_session (deleted in c4496114, crate-jmap-metadata-client/src/lib.rs:14-36)
